expectations.text: The firmware computes spin direction as a sensor axis plus sign (e.g. from integrated gyro rotation and/or cross products of consecutive samples) and sends it in the BLE packet
The firmware handles both twisting around the device's own axis and circular wrist motion where the gyro vector rotates
expectations.evidence: twist, gyro circle and accel circle methods

expectations.text: The firmware reports when the direction is unknown/ambiguous (e.g. a confidence flag or threshold) rather than always guessing
expectations.evidence: bit6 known flag with strength/share thresholds

expectations.text: The game learns which axis+sign means clockwise for this device and grip through a calibration step where the player spins in a known direction
expectations.evidence: spinSetup learns CW then CCW from 45 packets, 70% agreement

expectations.text: The calibration result is stored per device (e.g. localStorage keyed by device name) so it is not repeated every session
The JS maps incoming direction to +1/-1/0 and the mini-game uses it to push the marker right/left
expectations.evidence: stickSpin returns -1/0/+1 and push; hold-fish.js moves marker

expectations.text: The solution includes keyboard keys for spinning clockwise and counter-clockwise so the mini-game can be tested without the stick
